$comment: ATA-2 bounds attenuation as a meet-semilattice: isWithin(child, parent) is true iff the child's bounds are no wider than the parent's, dimension by dimension. jurisdictions/disputeMethods attenuate by SUBSET (child ⊆ parent); caps attenuate by ≤ (decimal-integer base units); forbiddenClauseCategories attenuates by SUPERSET (child ⊇ parent — a restriction set attenuates by forbidding MORE, so a child that DROPS a parent's forbidden category has WIDENED). A parent dimension left undefined is unbounded (child always within). Any unrecognized bound key fails closed. Same predicate serves ATA-4's commitment-vs-leaf containment. Authored FROM THE ATA-2 SEMANTICS (the deepening gate's net-new vector — never derived from bounds.ts).

cases.name: empty child within an EMPTY (unbounded) parent — nothing restricts, within
empty child does NOT escape a restricting parent — absent dimension = unbounded = wider (the forged-empty-link)
child omitting ONE restricted dimension is rejected (partial escape — caps present but jurisdictions absent)
explicit empty caps ({}) is MORE restrictive than a capped parent — within
jurisdictions subset (child ⊆ parent)
jurisdiction not in parent — widened, reject
caps ≤ parent (decimal-integer base units)
caps equal is within
the forged-widening case — a $10k grant delegating a $50M link MUST reject
cap currency not authorized by parent — reject
big-integer cap comparison (beyond Number precision) within
non-integer cap string fails closed
disputeMethods subset (narrowing acceptable methods)
disputeMethod not in parent — reject
forbiddenClauseCategories SUPERSET (child forbids more) is within — the inverted direction
forbiddenClauseCategories equal is within
forbiddenClauseCategories DROPS a parent category — WIDENED, reject (a subset-for-both impl wrongly accepts this)
forbiddenClauseCategories child forbids nothing while parent forbids one — reject
parent leaves a dimension unbounded — child within
all four dimensions valid together
one bad dimension among valid ones fails the whole (cap exceeds)
unknown bound key in child fails closed
unknown bound key in parent fails closed
ATA-4 commitment within leaf grant bounds
ATA-4 commitment EXCEEDS leaf grant — reject (the walk would otherwise affirm a chain-valid acceptance the grant never covered)
P4 two-hop chain — the officer link WIDENS the org's caps (5x) → non-attenuating, reject (authority-producer-ref widening guard)
cases.$comment: The Task-4 non-attenuating officer link on a real chain (org → officer → agent): the officer's link grants a cap the org never held (5000000 > 1000000). isWithin(officerBounds, orgBounds) MUST be false so the chain walk fails rather than affirming a forged deeper authority. produceDelegationLink refuses to MINT this link at issuance (linkAttenuates false); the verifier rejects it if presented.

cases.name: P4 two-hop chain — the officer link ADDS a dispute method the org never held → non-attenuating, reject
cases.$comment: A subtler non-attenuating officer link: caps and jurisdictions attenuate, but disputeMethods WIDENS (adds 'litigation' the org's grant never permitted). isWithin MUST reject on the disputeMethods dimension alone — a chain that narrows money but widens the acceptable forum is still an escape.

cases.name: P4 commitment-exceeds-grant on the four-dimension leaf — commitment adds a jurisdiction the leaf never granted → reject
cases.$comment: ATA-4 containment on the produced leaf: an acceptance whose commitment claims a jurisdiction (US-NY) outside the leaf grant's single jurisdiction (US-DE) exceeds the grant. commitmentWithinLeaf (isWithin) MUST reject — the record commits to more than the grant covers.
